tasks.title: Add the v2 file contracts: state/v2, iteration/v2, session/v2, gate-verdict/v1 and metrics/v2
tasks.goal: Every later task writes or reads one of these shapes, so they come first and are pure additions (brief G1, G6, G7, G8; Shape step 1). Each is its v1 with exactly the changes the brief lists and no others; the v1 schemas stay embedded because metrics and `vloop status` keep reading v1 records. Nothing in Go switches to the new shapes here — that is T4 onward.

references.why: the plan state/v2 versions: v2 is v1 with no task files, task and gate_history fixtures, and plan checks, gate_scratch and gate_review — nothing else changes
the iteration record iteration/v2 versions: outcome gains check_failed and the record gains checks [{name, exit, duration_ms}]
the session record session/v2 versions: the phase gains gate-review, a gate-review record has iteration 0 and no task
the shape gate-verdict/v1 starts from: verdict PASS or FAIL, findings with summary and kind, notes — but no top-level task and a per-task list
P-3 and P-4: the task fields and gate_history the schema encodes

acceptance: `vloop schema list` lists state/v2, iteration/v2, session/v2, gate-verdict/v1 and metrics/v2 alongside every v1 schema, which are unchanged byte for byte.

schemas/state.v2.json is state/v1 with exactly these changes: a task has no `files`; a task gains `fixtures` (a string, "" when there is no gate folder); a gate_history entry gains `fixtures`; the plan gains `checks` ([{name, paths, run}]), `gate_scratch` (a list of strings) and `gate_review` ({rounds 0–2, verdict PASS, FAIL or ""}); task.model and task.effort stay {work, review}.
schemas/iteration.v2.json is iteration/v1 with `check_failed` added to the outcome enum and `checks` ([{name, exit, duration_ms}]) added; nothing else differs.
schemas/session.v2.json is session/v1 with `gate-review` added to the phase enum; a gate-review record, like a plan record, carries no `task`.

schemas/gate-verdict.v1.json has no top-level `task`, a `verdict` of PASS or FAIL, `tasks` with one {task, verdict, findings: [{summary, kind}]} entry per task, and `notes`; the finding kinds are exactly wrong-reason, not-contract, task-reach, unpassable and pins-unnamed.
schemas/metrics.v2.json is metrics/v1 with time gaining checks_ms and gate_review_ms and every per-phase object (cost, models, effort, missing records) gaining gate-review; no other key changes.
internal/schema tests validate a passing and a failing document for each new schema.

tasks.title: Add the [[check]] tables, run.gate-scratch and the gate-review model and effort keys to config
tasks.goal: Checks, gate scratch folders and the gate-review session are all configured, so the keys exist before anything consumes them (brief G4, G3, G6; Shape step 2). `[[check]]` is the first table-array in the config file: `vloop config set` must keep it intact when it rewrites the file, and a malformed check must be refused like any other bad config value. `docs/guide/configuration.md` documents every new key here, because this task defines them.

references.why: every config key is documented here; [[check]], run.gate-scratch, model.gate-review and effort.gate-review join it in the existing format
C- invariants: how config is read and that a bad file value is a problem; P-7 (new) is what checks are for

acceptance: `[[check]]` tables are read from .vloop/config.toml, each with `name` (unique, matching [a-z0-9-]+), `paths` (a non-empty list of repo-relative globs in the metrics glob syntax) and `run` (one command); a duplicate name, a bad name, empty paths or a missing run makes reading the config fail with a `vloop: ` message, as other bad config values do.
`vloop config list` prints each check, in config order, as `check.<name>=<run> (paths: <globs>)`, after the existing keys' lines.

`run.gate-scratch` is a list key (default empty), `model.gate-review` defaults to `sonnet`, and `effort.gate-review` takes the effort values; all three work with `vloop config get`, `set` and `list` like their siblings.
There is no environment override for checks.
`vloop config set` of any key leaves the file's [[check]] tables in place.
docs/guide/configuration.md documents [[check]], run.gate-scratch, model.gate-review and effort.gate-review.
Config tests cover each new key and each refusal.

tasks.title: Write starter checks in vloop init and upgrade, and make doctor report no check and an un-ignored scratch folder
tasks.goal: A repository needs at least one check before vloop 2 will run it, so init and upgrade write starting points per detected stack and doctor names what is missing (brief G9; Shape step 2). Doctor is also run's preflight, so once no-check is a problem every test repository that runs `vloop run` needs a passing check: the run harness in cmd/vloop (newRunRepo and every test that builds its own run repository) gains `[[check]] name, paths = ["**"], run = "true"` here, which is the brief's stated change for those tests.

references.why: the [[check]] format init and upgrade write
Setting up a repository: what init writes and says
C- invariants on config, and P-7 (new): a plan has at least one check

acceptance: `vloop init` writes one [[check]] per detected stack: for an unscoped `go` stack `run = "go test ./... && go vet ./..."` with `paths = ["**"]`; a scoped stack `<stack>@<dir>` gets `paths = ["<dir>/**"]`; other stacks get their usual test command; init's output says each check is a starting point.
`vloop upgrade` to a 2.x binary from 1.x is refused without --yes as today; with --yes it adds the same checks when none are configured and shows them; it never touches an existing [[check]].
`vloop doctor` reports a missing [[check]] as a problem and a run.gate-scratch folder git does not ignore as a problem.
Every cmd/vloop test that runs `vloop run` has a passing [[check]] in its config (`run = "true"`, `paths = ["**"]`), and nothing else about those tests changes in this task.
Tests cover init per stack and scope, the upgrade addition and its refusal, and both doctor problems.

tasks.goal: A gate's judge may be files, not only a command, and those files must be as far out of a task's reach as the plan itself (brief G2). tasks.title: Empty the gate scratch folders after every gate, fail a gate that changes the tree, and stop re-running a timed-out gate
tasks.goal: Oracle tests run by the product's own runner have to sit inside the product, so a gate copies them into a git-ignored scratch folder named in config; the driver, not each gate, cleans up, so a crashed gate's copy cannot ride into a commit through `git add -A` (brief G3). A gate that changes anything else in the tree fails, restored. A timed-out gate is no longer re-run: it cost twice its limit. The timeout scenario in the gate runs only when this task's own gate runs (it needs a full minute).

references.why: R-4: every gate runs under a timeout and leaves no process behind; S-3: what the driver restores
the iteration and the run folder: where gate logs go and what a gate may leave
The gate: what a gate may touch

acceptance: `vloop run` refuses before planning when a run.gate-scratch folder is not ignored by git: `vloop: gate scratch <path> is not ignored by git — add it to .gitignore` (exit 1), starting no session; the plan copies the list into gate_scratch.
After every gate run — in `vloop run`, at acceptance and in `vloop task gate` — the driver removes everything inside each scratch folder.

The driver snapshots the tree before each gate and compares after, ignoring .vloop/tmp/ and the scratch folders; a gate that changed anything has it restored and fails, its log ending `vloop: gate T<n> changed the tree — restored: <paths>`.
A timed-out gate is not re-run; the one immediate re-run stays for an ordinary failure. TestRunFlakyGate and TestWorkedExampleB6FlakyGate gain the timeout case and change nothing else.
Tests cover the scratch refusal, the emptying in each of the three places, the tree restore of a new and of a modified file, and the timeout.

tasks.goal: Scoped checks are the repository's regression net once gates stop running suites (brief G4 after-iteration and final pass, G7). After an iteration whose gates all passed, the driver runs the checks whose globs match what the iteration changed, including untracked files; a failure costs an attempt and skips the review. When the last task is done every check runs once more, which catches what no single iteration's scope saw. A check owns its flakes and is never re-run — that is a violation the review rules on. The review session is told the checks' results and log paths.

A failing check ends the iteration as `check_failed`: no review, attempts+1, the note names the check and its log; a check is never re-run for flakiness.
Logs are checks/<name>.log (latest) and checks/<iteration>-<name>.fail.log, the iteration zero-padded as gate fail logs are; final-pass logs are checks/final-<name>.log.

The review session is given the checks' results and log paths and is not asked to re-run the tests.

tasks.title: Move metrics to metrics/v2 with check and gate-review time, and derive a defect from each check failure
tasks.goal: The new phase and the checks cost time and money, and a check failure is a defect the loop caught; metrics must count them without disturbing what B1–B8 already report (brief G8). v1 records are still read; closed briefs' snapshots stay metrics/v1. The gate's real-data check compares every consumed brief's metrics against a build of the plan's base commit, less `schema` and the keys metrics/v2 adds.

references.why: time, phases and defects: the definitions checks_ms, gate_review_ms and the check-failure defect must follow
M-1 (recomputed from raw sources, unrounded sums) and M-4 (how a failure is blamed)

acceptance: `vloop metrics --json` emits metrics/v2: time gains checks_ms and gate_review_ms; every per-phase object (cost, models, effort, missing records) gains gate-review; a check failure is a derived defect origin work, found-by gate, kind regression; the export's catchers do not change and defect/v1 and export/v1 do not version.
For every consumed brief (B1–B8), the new binary's metrics less `schema` and the added keys equal v1.0.0's output exactly; v1 records remain readable.
Closed briefs' snapshots under .vloop/state/metrics/ stay metrics/v1 and are not rewritten.
Metrics and snapshot tests follow metrics/v2 and cover check time, gate-review time and the check-failure defect.

This task adds the worked example as an e2e test, each line a case that fails on the base, and its gate runs the whole suite, the toolchain checks, the real-data metrics comparison against the plan's base and `vloop status` on B8's committed state/v1 plan.

references.why: R-3: the exit codes the worked example pins
the iteration and endings the worked example walks through

acceptance: cmd/vloop/b9_e2e_test.go plays every line of the brief's worked example with the stub claude in a temp repo, using the sh shell and the config the example gives, and asserts its exit codes, messages and effects; each case fails against the plan's base; it uses no absolute path in anything it commits.
go test ./... passes, as do gofmt -l ., go vet ./..., go mod tidy -diff and the linux and windows builds.
On this repository, vloop metrics --json for every consumed brief (B1–B8) from a build of the tree equals a build of the plan's base, less schema and the keys metrics/v2 adds.
vloop status reads B8's committed state/v1 plan.
